questions.stem: Which of the following defines SIGINT?
questions.key: Intelligence gathering by interception of signals, whether communications between people or electronic signals not directly used in communication
distractors: Intelligence gathering from people through interviews, debriefing and direct contact with sources
Intelligence gathering from imagery taken by aerial and satellite sensors over the area of operations
Intelligence gathering from openly available publications, broadcasts and public records
questions.explanation: The lesson defines SIGINT as intelligence gathering by interception of signals, either communications (COMINT) between people or electronic (ELINT) signals not directly used in communication.
why: That describes human-source intelligence, not interception of signals.
That describes imagery intelligence; SIGINT works from intercepted signals, not images.
SIGINT is not built from open publications; it intercepts communications and electronic signals.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes Communication Intelligence (COMINT)?
questions.key: Dealing with messages or voice information derived from the interception of foreign communication
distractors: Gathering intelligence by use of electronic sensors and various electronic surveillance systems
Converting collected SIGINT data into intelligence through analysis
Providing real time intelligence to the infantry brigades and battalions in support of AFP missions
questions.explanation: COMINT deals with messages or voice information derived from interception of foreign communication, and can reveal who is transmitting, location, text and voice.
why: That is the lesson's description of ELINT, the other SIGINT category.
That describes the Analysis step of the SIGINT cycle, not a category of SIGINT.
That is the general objective of the PA SIGINT program, not the meaning of COMINT.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes Electronic Intelligence (ELINT)?
questions.key: Intelligence gathering by use of electronic sensors and various electronic surveillance systems
distractors: Dealing with messages or voice information derived from the interception of foreign communication
Using cryptanalysis to decipher messages and traffic analysis to re-integrate information
Monitoring enemy activities and locating their estimated locations with a receiver and bearing processor
questions.explanation: ELINT is intelligence gathering by electronic sensors and electronic surveillance systems, as opposed to COMINT, which deals with messages and voice.
why: That is COMINT, the other SIGINT category.
Cryptanalysis and traffic analysis are described as part of SIGINT in general because sensitive information is often encrypted, not as the definition of ELINT.
That describes the Radio Direction Finder System, a SIGINT capability of Army units.

questions.stem: Which of the following defines intelligence?
questions.key: The product resulting from the collection, evaluation, analysis and integration of all available information on foreign nations or areas of operations that is significant to military planning
distractors: The gathering of raw information from every available source without evaluation or analysis
The interception of signals, whether communications between people or electronic emissions
The timely production of information for those who need to know only
questions.explanation: Intelligence is the product of collection, evaluation, analysis and integration of all available information that is immediately or potentially significant to military planning and operations.
why: Raw information is only the input; intelligence is the product after evaluation, analysis and integration.
That is the definition of SIGINT, one kind of intelligence gathering.
That describes dissemination, the last step of the SIGINT cycle.

questions.stem: It is the SIGINT cycle step in which operators must understand the mission and the direction needs in order to plan and apply appropriate collection mechanisms.
questions.explanation: Requirements is the first step: operators must understand the mission and direction needs so they can plan and apply appropriate collection mechanisms.
why: Collection is the proper procedure of gathering information, which follows once requirements are understood.
Processing/Exploitation deals with intercepted traffic and the estimated direction of the enemy.
Dissemination is the timely production of intelligence to those who need to know only.

questions.stem: It is the SIGINT cycle step that converts collected SIGINT data into intelligence.
questions.explanation: Analysis is defined as converting collected SIGINT data into intelligence.
why: Collection is the proper procedure of gathering information, not the conversion into intelligence.
Processing/Exploitation covers intercepted communication traffic and the estimated direction of the enemy.
Requirements is about understanding the mission and direction needs before collecting.

questions.stem: This SIGINT capability of Army units, made up of a Doppler antenna and a radio receiver and bearing processor, is used for radio communication transmission countermeasures to monitor enemy activities and locate their estimated locations.
questions.explanation: Slide 17: the Radio Direction Finder System, with a Doppler antenna and a radio receiver and bearing processor, is used for radio communication transmission countermeasures to monitor enemy activities and locate their estimated locations.
why: COMINT is a SIGINT category dealing with messages or voice from intercepted communication, not this antenna-and-processor system.
ELINT is a SIGINT category using electronic sensors and surveillance systems, not this antenna-and-processor system.
Cryptanalysis is a technique for deciphering encrypted messages, not a direction-finding system.

questions.stem: A SIGINT team reports the intercepted communication traffic and the estimated direction of the enemy to its section leader. Which step of the SIGINT cycle is being performed?
questions.explanation: Processing/Exploitation is the step that handles intercepted communication traffic and the estimated direction of the enemy.
why: Analysis converts the collected data into intelligence, a later step.
Collection is gathering the information in the first place.
Dissemination is timely production of intelligence for those who need to know.

questions.stem: A SIGINT section sends its finished intelligence promptly, but only to the units that need to know it. Which step of the SIGINT cycle does this describe?
questions.explanation: Dissemination is the timely production of intelligence to those who need to know only.
why: Requirements means understanding the mission and direction needs.
Collection is the proper procedure of gathering information.
Analysis converts collected data into intelligence before it is sent out.

questions.stem: Analysts cannot ask the sender of an intercepted message what it meant. Which statement from the lesson does this reflect?
questions.key: SIGINT cannot be clarified from the source
distractors: SIGINT involves cryptanalysis to decipher encrypted messages
If security is compromised, the enemy can counter with disinformation or deception
SIGINT is accurate, timely and relevant
questions.explanation: Slide 20 lists as a disadvantage that SIGINT cannot be clarified from the source: the sender of an intercept cannot be asked what it meant.
why: Cryptanalysis is a technique described on slide 13 for encrypted messages, not a statement about asking the sender.
This disadvantage concerns enemy deception after a security compromise, not asking the sender.
These are the advantages of SIGINT, not a limitation.

questions.stem: A unit learns that the enemy knows how its intercept effort works and is now feeding it false traffic. Which disadvantage of SIGINT does this describe?
questions.key: If security is compromised, the enemy can counter the government efforts with disinformation or deception
distractors: SIGINT cannot be clarified from the source
SIGINT sometimes cannot stand alone without substantiation from other intelligence disciplines
SIGINT is accurate, timely and relevant
questions.explanation: Slide 20: if security is compromised, the enemy can counter the government's efforts with disinformation or deception.
why: This disadvantage is about being unable to ask the sender what a message meant.
This disadvantage is about needing substantiation from other disciplines, not enemy deception.
These are the advantages of SIGINT, not a disadvantage.

questions.stem: Which list contains the three advantages of SIGINT?
questions.explanation: The lesson lists SIGINT's advantages as Accurate, Timely and Relevant.
why: Complete is not one of the three advantages.
Secure is not one of the listed advantages; security appears among the disadvantages.
Verified is not an advantage in the lesson, and Accurate is missing.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a step of the SIGINT cycle?
questions.explanation: The cycle steps are Requirements, Collection, Processing/Exploitation, Analysis and Dissemination. Cryptanalysis is mentioned as a technique used in SIGINT, not as a cycle step.
why: Collection is the second step of the cycle.
Analysis is the fourth step of the cycle.
Dissemination is the last step of the cycle.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT something COMINT is capable of revealing?
questions.explanation: COMINT can reveal who is transmitting, location, text interception and voice interception. Jamming is listed among ELINT's capabilities.
why: Who is transmitting is a listed COMINT capability.
Text interception is a listed COMINT capability.
Voice interception is a listed COMINT capability.
